title: Appeal of RE In Mo Chung v. Korean Capital Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained; the Presbytery's and/or its Special Judicial Commission's actions in assuming original jurisdiction and adjudicating charges against RE In Mo Chung, including the excommunication, are reversed.
first_summary: In an appeal from excommunication, the SJC addressed whether a presbytery and its special judicial commission could receive and adjudicate charges against a church member. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed, holding that the local session is the court of original jurisdiction for communicant members. Because the appellant was a member of Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington, the presbytery and commission acted contrary to constitutional standards. No remand was ordered.
summary: The SJC decided whether a presbytery and its special judicial commission could assume original jurisdiction over disciplinary charges against a church member. It sustained the appeal and reversed: the court of original jurisdiction for communicant members is the local church session. Because the appellant was a member of Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington, the presbytery and its commission acted contrary to constitutional standards when they adjudicated the charges and imposed excommunication. The ruling rested on jurisdiction, not the merits; no remand was ordered.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2001-15, Standing Judicial Commission, 30th General Assembly (2002), source lines 1–5, 14. A five-member panel decided the appeal on Dec. 5, 2001; the Statement of Issue and Judgment were prepared and adopted by the panel, the Reasoning was written by TE Jim Smith with concurrence by four members, and the roll call adopted the decision with 16 concurred, 1 dissented, 1 recused, 1 disqualified, and 5 absent (lines 39, 64–66).
evidence_notes.dispute: Beginning in 1999, conflict in Korean Presbyterian Church Washington led Korean Capital Presbytery to suspend the session and appoint a commission; after a civil-court trustees petition and member accusations, the commission summoned RE Chung, found him guilty of contumacy and making a false statement, and imposed excommunication, which KCP approved on Apr. 2, 2001 (lines 18–35).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The issue was whether the Presbytery and/or its Jan. 8, 2001 Special Judicial Commission was the proper court to assume original jurisdiction over charges against the appellant. Judgment: No; original jurisdiction belongs to the Session, so the Presbytery's and/or Commission's actions are reversed. Reasoning: the court of original jurisdiction for communicant members is the local session, and the appellant was a member of KPCW, so any judicial action or censure had to originate there; the commission acted contrary to constitutional standards (lines 41–62).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The Statement of Facts was prepared by RE John White; the Statement of Issue and Judgment were adopted by the five-member panel; the Reasoning was authored by TE Jim Smith with concurrence by TE Charles McGowan, RE Grant McCabe, RE John White, and RE Jack Williamson; the roll call records one dissent by RE Howard Donahoe, with others absent, recused, or disqualified (lines 64–66).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: None. No incorporated decision is identified; the roll call notes a dissent but no separate dissent opinion is supplied (line 66).
